Output and visualization API ​

Output defines snapshot capture and persistence. Observations owns observation sampling ([output.observations]: point events and station series sampled at met-window ends). Visualization provides topology-aware field views and optional Makie rendering for those snapshots.

Output ​

AtmosTransport.Output Module
julia
Output

Topology-aware diagnostic output for AtmosTransport runtime products.

This module owns the public NetCDF output contract. Runtime code should capture model state with capture_snapshot and write files with write_snapshot_netcdf instead of defining ad-hoc NetCDF layouts in runner code.

The writer is intentionally topology-dispatched:

  • LatLonMesh writes regular CF lon/lat coordinates.

  • ReducedGaussianMesh writes native cell-indexed diagnostics plus a legacy lon/lat raster view for current debug plots.

  • CubedSphereMesh writes panel-native diagnostics with GEOS-style lons, lats, corner_lons, corner_lats, cell_area, and cubed_sphere metadata so Panoply and downstream tools have enough geometry context to render C-grid snapshots.

New topologies should add methods for the small internal schema/diagnostic functions in this folder; they should not special-case the runner.

Observation sampling lives in AtmosTransport.Observations.

source
AtmosTransport.Output.RuntimeOutputMetadata Type

Metadata resolved from the typed physics objects of one runtime invocation.

source
AtmosTransport.Output.SelectedSnapshotFrame Type
julia
SelectedSnapshotFrame

CPU-resident output containing only requested levels and column reductions. nlevel preserves the original vertical coordinate. levels maps stored layers back to model levels; column sums are computed before selecting layers. Tracer storage is VMR × air mass, with no molecular-weight conversion.

source
AtmosTransport.Output.SnapshotFrame Type
julia
SnapshotFrame

CPU-resident snapshot of one model state at one output time.

air_mass and each entry in tracers keep the topology-native storage shape:

  • LL: (lon, lat, lev)

  • RG: (cell, lev)

  • CS: NTuple{6, Array{T, 3}} with panel interiors (Xdim, Ydim, lev)

Tracer arrays store the model's conservative χ × carrier-air-mass quantity, not mixing ratio or physical kg species. Derived VMR and column diagnostics are computed by write_snapshot_netcdf. tracer_total_mass stores a compensated Float64 sum of that conservative quantity for every tracer. It is kept separately so Float32 visualization payloads cannot degrade global signed mass diagnostics through cancellation or output conversion.

Snapshot storage must be CPU-resident. Use capture_snapshot for model state on any backend; it strips cubed-sphere halos and copies device arrays to the host before constructing the frame.

source
AtmosTransport.Output.SnapshotWriteOptions Type
julia
SnapshotWriteOptions(; float_type=Float32, deflate_level=0, shuffle=true)

Options controlling NetCDF snapshot output.

  • float_type is the on-disk type for heavy diagnostic variables.

  • deflate_level is the NetCDF compression level for heavy payload variables: 0 disables compression, 1 is fast/light, and 9 is maximum compression.

  • shuffle enables the NetCDF shuffle filter when compression is active.

source
AtmosTransport.Output.capture_snapshot Method
julia
capture_snapshot(model; time_hours=0, halo_width=0, fields=nothing)

Capture air-mass and conservative tracer-storage fields from a TransportModel. Without fields, return a full SnapshotFrame. Passing an OutputFieldSpec returns a SelectedSnapshotFrame containing only requested layers and column diagnostics, plus compensated Float64 totals for the selected tracers.

The result is CPU-resident and topology-native. For cubed-sphere states, halo_width strips panel halos before writing. GPU-backed arrays are copied to host memory by Array(...).

source
AtmosTransport.Output.check_output_targets Method
julia
check_output_targets(spec, output_cfg)

Reject snapshot settings that would silently write nothing while [output].enabled is true: a path without any snapshot-schedule key, or snapshot times without a path. An explicitly empty list (hours = []) is a deliberate "no snapshots" (the path then only names the timing CSV of ATMOSTR_TIMERS runs).

source
AtmosTransport.Output.column_mean_mixing_ratio Method
julia
column_mean_mixing_ratio(air_mass, tracer_storage)

Compute the air-mass-weighted vertical mean mixing ratio for one snapshot field.

The returned shape is topology-native horizontal storage:

  • LL: (lon, lat)

  • RG: (cell,)

  • CS: NTuple{6, Matrix{Float64}}

source
AtmosTransport.Output.define_cs_horizontal_geometry! Method
julia
define_cs_horizontal_geometry!(ds, mesh::CubedSphereMesh) -> nothing

Define the horizontal geometry of a panel-native cubed-sphere NetCDF file in the open dataset ds: the GEOS-style layout shared by runtime snapshots and cs_native input files. Vertical and time axes are not defined here; each writer owns those.

Dimensions Xdim, Ydim (Nc), Xcorner, Ycorner (Nc + 1) and nf (6). Variables (coordinates and geometry in Float64 whatever the mesh precision):

  • Xdim, Ydim: panel indices 1:Nc, tagged degrees_east/degrees_north ("Fake Longitude/Latitude for GrADS Compatibility", the GEOS-Chem convention) so Panoply and GrADS render a per-panel map; nf (Int32): panel 1:6.

  • lons, lats (Xdim, Ydim, nf): cell-centre longitude and latitude [degrees], from panel_cell_center_lonlat in the mesh's panel convention.

  • corner_lons, corner_lats (Xcorner, Ycorner, nf): cell corners [degrees], from panel_cell_corner_lonlat.

  • cell_area (Xdim, Ydim, nf) [m²]: the mesh's own cell areas (the areas the runtime multiplies fluxes by), with coordinates = "lons lats".

  • cubed_sphere (scalar Int32): grid mapping with grid_mapping_name, cs_definition, cs_coordinate_law, cs_center_law, panel_convention, longitude_of_central_meridian, semi_major_axis = mesh.radius [m] and inverse_flattening = 0. Panel data variables point at it with grid_mapping = "cubed_sphere" and coordinates = "lons lats".

The same definition tags are also written as global attributes (Nc, cs_definition, cs_coordinate_law, cs_center_law, panel_convention, grid_mapping_name, longitude_of_central_meridian); readers rebuild the mesh from them.

AtmosTransport.Output.define_product_attributes! Method
julia
define_product_attributes!(ds, mesh, mass_basis, title, contract)

Write the ordered common NetCDF attributes shared by snapshots and observations. Product-specific metadata and provenance are written by the caller afterward.

source
AtmosTransport.Output.define_provenance_attributes! Method
julia
define_provenance_attributes!(ds) -> (; creation_date, git_commit, git_dirty)

Write the automated provenance block shared by every NetCDF file AtmosTransport writes (snapshots, observation files, and generated input files) as global attributes of the open dataset ds:

AttributeValue
creation_datewrite time, ISO 8601 UTC with a Z suffix
framework"AtmosTransport.jl"
framework_commitcommit of the source tree (AtmosTransport.source_revision())
framework_dirty"clean", "dirty" or "unknown"
runtimeJulia version, machine triple and operating system
hostname, userhost name and USER (or USERNAME)

Every value is best-effort and falls back to "unknown" instead of throwing, so a tree without git still produces a complete block. Returns the creation date and the source-tree state so the caller can compose its history line.

AtmosTransport.Output.with_netcdf_lock Method
julia
with_netcdf_lock(f)

Run f() holding the process-wide NetCDF lock. Every runtime NetCDF write (snapshot files, the snapshot stream, observation streams) goes through it, because netcdf-c is not thread-safe and daily snapshot files are written on a background task.

source
AtmosTransport.Output.write_snapshot_binary Method
julia
write_snapshot_binary(path, frames, grid; mass_basis=:dry, options=SnapshotWriteOptions(),
                      physics_attributes=Dict())

Write CS snapshots to a self-describing binary file. Skips NetCDF library overhead entirely; pair with scripts/postprocess/binary_to_netcdf.jl for the offline conversion. Throws if grid.horizontal is not a CubedSphereMesh.

source
AtmosTransport.Output.write_snapshot_netcdf Method
julia
write_snapshot_netcdf(path, frames, grid; mass_basis=:dry, options=SnapshotWriteOptions(),
                      fields=output_field_spec(), physics_attributes=Dict())

Write topology-aware runtime snapshots to NetCDF.

By default the output contains full per-level VMR fields, stored air mass, layer mass-per-area diagnostics, column air mass per area, and tracer column means; fields (an OutputFieldSpec) selects tracers, layers and diagnostics. Every written tracer also gets its Float64 <tracer>_total_mass(time). Reduced-Gaussian files also carry a legacy lon/lat raster view for quick plots. Cubed-sphere files carry panel lon/lat coordinates and a cubed_sphere grid-mapping variable modeled after GEOS-Chem diagnostics.

Observations ​

Import sampling and retrieval APIs from AtmosTransport.Observations. Its Retrievals, Sources and Sampling submodules separate the column operator, input records and runtime sampling. Their public names are re-exported by Observations.

AtmosTransport.Observations Module

Observation sources, retrieval columns, placement, sampling and NetCDF sinks.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Retrievals Module

Retrievals for observation columns and sampling.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Retrievals.AbstractRetrievalMapping Type
julia
AbstractRetrievalMapping

How the profile values of a retrieval relate to its pressures, and so how the model column is mapped onto them (the projection matrix P of retrieval_column_weights!): LayerRebin (values are layer means between interfaces) or HatLevelProjection (values on levels, the profile linear in pressure between them). A RetrievalColumn carries one; the operator dispatches on it.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Retrievals.HatLevelProjection Type
julia
HatLevelProjection()

Retrieval values sit on N levels and the profile is linear in pressure between them: the OCO-2 and OCO-3 retrievals (20 levels, "defined on layer boundaries", the first at σ=10−4), whose pressure weights are the integrals of the levels' hat functions (the trapezoid rule with half-thickness end levels, with a dry-air correction). The model column, stretched onto the retrieval levels (top level to bottom level), is projected onto the retrieval's basis, the hat functions φj of the levels (φj(pj)=1, linear to 0 at the neighbouring levels): the level values c are the L2 (Galerkin) projection in dry air,

∑iMjici=bj,Mji=∫φjφidpdry,bj=∫φjxdpdry=∑kBjkxk,Bjk=mkΔsk∫sk−1/2sk+1/2φj(p)dp,

so P=M−1B, with each stretched model layer k (air mass mk, the run's dry air mass by default) spread evenly over its pressure thickness Δsk; M is tridiagonal. The hats sum to 1 over the stretched column, so the rows of P sum to 1 and, with the hat integrals hj=∑kBjk/∑kmk as weights, ∑jhjcj is the model's air-mass-weighted column mean: the projection conserves the column. It reproduces every profile the retrieval can represent (piecewise linear on the levels), to the discretization of the model's layer means. P, the inverse of the consistent mass matrix times B, has negative entries in general (about −0.2 in every row on a GEOS L72 column); the weights H=(h∘a)TP of OCO-2 retrievals stayed positive in the cases measured. Stored as retrieval_mapping = "hat_levels".

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Retrievals.LayerRebin Type
julia
LayerRebin()

Retrieval values are means over N layers between N + 1 interfaces (a TCCON or GOSAT layer grid, TM5-4DVar's 19-layer form of OCO-2, tm5_layer_column). The model column, stretched onto the retrieval column, is rebinned by pressure overlap: P=R, TM5-4DVar's mass-conserving inv_rebin (pressure-overlap rebin). Stored as retrieval_mapping = "layer_rebin".

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Retrievals.RetrievalColumn Type
julia
RetrievalColumn(pressure_pa, pressure_weight, averaging_kernel, prior_profile,
                profile_sigma, surface_pressure_pa[, mapping = LayerRebin()[, prior_column = NaN]])
RetrievalColumn(; pressure_pa, pressure_weight, averaging_kernel, prior_profile,
                  profile_sigma = Float64[], surface_pressure_pa = first(pressure_pa),
                  mapping = LayerRebin(), prior_column = NaN)

The vertical description of one retrieved column average (a satellite or TCCON sounding) with N retrieval values, ordered from the surface up. The mapping (AbstractRetrievalMapping) says what the values are:

  • LayerRebin: means over N layers; pressure_pa holds the N + 1 layer interfaces;

  • HatLevelProjection: values on N ≥ 2 levels, the profile linear in pressure between them (OCO-2/OCO-3); pressure_pa holds the N level pressures.

Fields:

  • pressure_pa: the interfaces or levels (Pa, total pressure), surface first, strictly decreasing; the last is the retrieval top (≥ 0);

  • pressure_weight: the pressure weights hi (N, ≥ 0, summing to 1 within RETRIEVAL_WEIGHT_SUM_TOLERANCE);

  • averaging_kernel: the column averaging kernel ai (N, normalized, dimensionless: ∂X/∂xi=hiai);

  • prior_profile: the retrieval prior xa,i (N, dry mole fraction, mol mol⁻¹, in [0, 1]);

  • profile_sigma: optional 1-σ uncertainty σi of the model profile on the retrieval layers or levels (N, mol mol⁻¹, in [0, 1]; empty when absent), the input of the model-error term retrieval_model_error_variance. It is not the retrieval's a-priori uncertainty: the smoothing error is already represented by the averaging kernel;

  • surface_pressure_pa: the retrieval surface pressure (Pa), equal to the first pressure (relative tolerance 1e-6);

  • mapping: the AbstractRetrievalMapping;

  • prior_column: optional, the retrieval's prior column Xa (mol mol⁻¹, in [0, 1]; NaN when absent), e.g. the OCO-2 xco2_apriori. When given, the column is X=Xa+∑ihiai((Px)i−xa,i) (the MIP protocol's eq. 2); without it Xa=∑ihixa,i. The two differ when the weights and the prior were averaged separately (OCO-2 10-s averages: a few thousandths of a ppm).

Every value but an absent prior_column must be finite. See retrieval_column_weights! for the operator.

oco2_level_form(mapping::AbstractRetrievalMapping, column::RetrievalColumn{HatLevelProjection})

A level retrieval (OCO-2/OCO-3) in the form the operator uses under mapping: unchanged for HatLevelProjection (the levels as given, the default), TM5-4DVar's 19 layers for LayerRebin (tm5_layer_column, the "tm5" mode).

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Retrievals.oco2_level_form_from_label Method
julia
oco2_level_form_from_label(label, context) -> AbstractRetrievalMapping

The mapping named "hat" (HatLevelProjection) or "tm5" (LayerRebin on TM5's 19 layers) in configs and on the command line.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Retrievals.retrieval_column_value Method
julia
retrieval_column_value(p_half, air, column::RetrievalColumn, x) -> Float64

The simulated column X=∑kHkxk+c of the model profile x (dry mole fraction, top first) on the model interface pressures p_half (Pa, top first, total pressures) and air masses air (read by the hat projection only; pass nothing for a LayerRebin column): retrieval_column_weights! and retrieval_prior_offset in one call.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Retrievals.retrieval_column_weights! Method
julia
retrieval_column_weights!(H, s, p_half, air, column::RetrievalColumn) -> H

Weights of the averaging-kernel column on the model layers: with the model profile xk (dry mole fraction, k = 1 at the top),

X=∑kHkxk+c,Hk=∑ihiaiPik,c=Xa−∑ihiaixa,i

(retrieval_prior_offset) with the column's prior column Xa (prior_column) when it gives one, Xa=∑ihixa,i (so c=∑ihi(1−ai)xa,i) when not. P maps the model column, stretched onto the retrieval column (stretch_model_interfaces!), onto the retrieval's values as its mapping says: the rebin R of LayerRebin (the column of TM5-4DVar's OCO-2 operator, averaging_kernels.F90, lines 228-235 and 245), or the hat projection of HatLevelProjection, which weights each model layer by its air mass air (kg per cell, top first; the run's dry air mass on a dry basis). Every row of P sums to 1 (dry-air projection). p_half are the model interface pressures (Pa, top first; total pressures, so that they compare with the retrieval's), s a scratch vector of the same length that receives the stretched interfaces. A layer column ignores air; pass nothing for it.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Retrievals.retrieval_layer_count Method
julia
retrieval_layer_count(column::RetrievalColumn) -> Int

Number of retrieval values of a RetrievalColumn: its layers (LayerRebin) or levels (HatLevelProjection).

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Retrievals.retrieval_mapping_label Method

The label of a mapping in observation files (retrieval_mapping).

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Retrievals.retrieval_model_error_variance Method
julia
retrieval_model_error_variance(column::RetrievalColumn) -> Float64

The model-error variance of the averaging-kernel column from the uncertainty σi of the model profile on the retrieval layers (profile_sigma), the layers taken independent: σmod2=∑i(hiaiσi)2, the operator's weights on the retrieval layers, squared, times the profile variance. Zero when the column gives no profile_sigma. It depends on the record only, so it is fixed for an inversion and the cost stays quadratic.

This is analogous to, not the same as, TM5-4DVar's model error: its CH4 TROPOMI routine (averaging_kernels.F90, line 669, and Satellite.py of the CH4 project) evaluates ∑kHk2σk2 with the weights H=(ha)R on the model layers and the spread of the modelled profiles σk from its track file, and its OCO-2 routine adds a column model error instead. profile_sigma is not the retrieval's a-priori uncertainty, whose effect (the smoothing error) the averaging kernel already represents.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Retrievals.retrieval_prior_offset Method
julia
retrieval_prior_offset(column::RetrievalColumn) -> Float64
retrieval_prior_offset(h, a, prior) -> Float64

The prior term of the averaging-kernel column, which does not depend on the model: c=Xa−∑ihiaixa,i with the column's prior_column Xa when it gives one (X=Xa+∑ihiai((Px)i−xa,i), the MIP protocol's form), else c=∑i(hi−hiai)xa,i (TM5: dot_product(pres_weights - W, prior_profile); the raw form always).

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Retrievals.retrieval_profile! Method
julia
retrieval_profile!(xr, s, p_half, air, column::RetrievalColumn, x) -> xr

The model profile x (top first) on the retrieval layers or levels (surface first), (Px)i: for a layer column the pressure-weighted mean over each retrieval layer, for a level column the hat projection, of the model column stretched onto the retrieval column (air as in retrieval_column_weights!; pass nothing for a LayerRebin column, which does not read it). s is scratch for the stretched interfaces. A diagnostic: the column itself is ∑ihiai(Px)i+c.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Retrievals.stretch_model_interfaces! Method
julia
stretch_model_interfaces!(s, p_half, surface_pa, top_pa) -> s

TM5-4DVar's stretch of the model column onto a retrieval column (averaging_kernels.F90, lines 213-219): the model interface pressures p_half (Pa, top first, p_half[end] the model surface pressure ps, p_half[1] the model top pt) mapped linearly so that the model surface falls on the retrieval surface psr (surface_pa) and the model top on the retrieval top ptr (top_pa),

sk=μpk+c,μ=psr−ptrps−pt,c=12[(psr−μps)+(ptr−μpt)].

Each model layer keeps its share Δpk/(ps−pt) of the column, so the pressure-weighted mean of any profile over the stretched layers is its mean over the model layers: the stretch moves the model column onto the retrieval's pressure range without adding or removing air.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Retrievals.tm5_layer_column Method
julia
tm5_layer_column(column::RetrievalColumn{HatLevelProjection}) -> RetrievalColumn{LayerRebin}

TM5-4DVar's layer form of a level retrieval (OCO-2/OCO-3 10-s files in proj/tracer/CO2/py/Observations.py, lines 7016-7052, used by Satellite.py, lines 707-717): the N levels become the interfaces of N − 1 layers, the averaging kernel and the prior are interpolated linearly in pressure to the layer midpoints (the mean of the two levels), and the pressure weights are the layer thicknesses Δpi, normalized to the column between the bottom and top levels. TM5 divides by the surface pressure instead, so its weights sum to 1−σtop (0.9999 for OCO-2) and its column is that fraction of this one. A profile_sigma is averaged like the kernel. The prior column is TM5's, ∑ihixa,i on its layers (a prior_column of the record is not carried). For comparisons with TM5-4DVAR; the hat projection (HatLevelProjection) is the consistent mapping of level retrievals.

AtmosTransport.Observations.Sources.AveragingKernelColumns Type
julia
AveragingKernelColumns(tracers, mapping = HatLevelProjection())

averaging_kernel_tracers = [...] on an oco2_lite source: the reader also reads each sounding's retrieval (levels, pressure weights, averaging kernel, prior, prior column; read_oco2_retrieval_columns), and the sampler writes, for each tracer of tracers, the averaging-kernel column X=Xa+∑ihiai((Px)i−xa,i) of the sampled profile as <tracer>_ak_column, with the operator of the 4D-Var (retrieval_column_weights!). mapping (averaging_kernel_mapping) is HatLevelProjection ("hat", the levels as given) or LayerRebin ("tm5", TM5-4DVar's 19 layers, tm5_layer_column). AtmosTransport.Observations.Sources.OCO2LiteSource Type
julia
OCO2LiteSource(path_template, quality_filter[, averaging_kernel = NoAveragingKernels()])

NASA OCO-2/OCO-3 Lite XCO2 files, or the OCO-2 v11 MIP 10-second average files (same sounding_id, time, latitude, longitude layout). Records passing quality_filter become point events. With averaging_kernel = AveragingKernelColumns(tracers) (opt-in) the reader also reads each record's retrieval and the sampler writes averaging-kernel columns of the named tracers (AveragingKernelColumns).

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sources.ObsPackSource Type
julia
ObsPackSource(path_template, mode, site_grouping)

NOAA ObsPack NetCDF dataset files. SiteMode() groups records into fixed stations by site_grouping; SoundingMode() samples every record at its own time.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sources.ObservationSet Type
julia
ObservationSet(origin, soundings, sites[, dropped_outside_window, skipped_invalid])

Every sampling request of a run. build_observation_set sorts soundings by time_seconds (stable) and merges sites so they are unique by id; the constructor itself neither sorts nor deduplicates, and only rejects site series with a TimeList schedule. dropped_outside_window counts the point events outside the transported span; skipped_invalid counts source rows skipped for fill values, invalid coordinates, or the quality filter.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sources.QualityFlagFilter Type
julia
QualityFlagFilter(variable, max)

quality_filter = "flag_max": keep records whose integer flag variable is <= max (Lite files: xco2_quality_flag, 0 = good).

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sources.QualityFlagValues Type
julia
QualityFlagValues(variable, values)

quality_filter = "flag_values": keep records whose integer flag variable is one of values. Use it for categorical flags such as the OCO-2 v11 MIP assimilate_flag (0 = not assimilated, 1 = assimilated, 2 = withheld), where <= max cannot select the wanted set.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sources.SiteCodeGrouping Type

One site per dataset file and distinct intake height. The id is the dataset name (ObsPack files already encode site, platform, and lab), suffixed with _<h>magl only when a file holds several intake heights.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sources.SiteMode Type

Fixed stations; written at every met-window end.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sources.SiteRequest Type
julia
SiteRequest(id, lon, lat, elevation_m, intake_height_m, source[, schedule[, altitude_m]])

A fixed station. The vertical fields have the meaning of those of SoundingRequest (NaN when unknown; a station has no pressure); the sampler turns them into a VerticalPlacement when it is built. schedule defaults to EveryWindow.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sources.SoundingMode Type

Time-stamped point events; each record is sampled at its own time.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sources.SoundingRequest Type
julia
SoundingRequest(id, time_seconds, lon, lat, source[, elevation_m, intake_height_m[, altitude_m, pressure_pa[,
                retrieval]]])

One point event, sampled at time_seconds after the run origin (Float64 UTC seconds). source indexes the spec's sources. The vertical fields are what the record says about its height, NaN when it says nothing: intake_height_m (m above the ground: the record's intake height, or its altitude minus its elevation), altitude_m (m above sea level), elevation_m (ground, m above sea level) and pressure_pa (Pa). The sampler turns them into a VerticalPlacement once, when it is built (resolve_placement). retrieval is the sounding's RetrievalColumn when its source asks for averaging-kernel columns (AveragingKernelColumns), else nothing.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sources.TOMLTableFormat Type

[[soundings]] or [[sites]] arrays of tables; times may be a TOML array.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sources.TableSource Type
julia
TableSource(path_template, mode, format)

Generic point list as CSV, TOML, or NetCDF. Point events need id, time (ISO-8601 UTC), lat, lon; sites need id, lat, lon. Both accept elevation (m asl) and intake_height (m above ground) or altitude (m asl, converted with elevation, else placed by resolve_placement). Sites may add start_time/end_time (TimeRange) or times (TimeList).

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sources.TimeList Type
julia
TimeList(times_seconds)

Sample the site once at each listed time (seconds after the run origin), like a sounding: blended between the bracketing met-window ends and written to the _soundings file with the intake-layer value.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sources.TimeRange Type
julia
TimeRange(start_seconds, stop_seconds)

Sample the site at every met-window end with start <= t <= stop (seconds after the run origin); records outside the range are written as NaN.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sources.averaging_kernel_tracers Method

The tracers whose averaging-kernel columns a source asks for (none by default).

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sources.build_observation_set Method
julia
build_observation_set(sources, origin, window_seconds) -> ObservationSet
build_observation_set(sources, origin, dates)

Read every source for the days covering the window, merge sites by id, expand site time lists into point events, keep the point events with window_seconds[1] <= t <= window_seconds[2] (seconds after origin; the dates form uses whole days), and sort them by time (stable). A site id that repeats (across rows, daily files, or sources) must keep its location; time lists of a repeated id are merged, and other schedules must be equal. Per-source counts are logged.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sources.expand_observation_paths Method
julia
expand_observation_paths(template, dates) -> Vector{String}

Resolve a source path template for the run days: {YYYYMMDD} (alias {date}), {YYMMDD}, {YYYY}, {MM}, {DD} are substituted per day and * / ? wildcards are expanded in the file name. Returns unique existing paths in order. A path without date tokens must match at least one file; templated paths may resolve to nothing on days without data.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sources.isvalid_lonlat Method
julia
isvalid_lonlat(lon, lat) -> Bool

Finite coordinates with |lat| ≤ 90 and |lon| ≤ 720: fill values such as -999999 are rejected while every ordinary longitude convention passes. Readers filter with this predicate; locate enforces it.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sources.observation_source_from_cfg Method
julia
observation_source_from_cfg(cfg, label) -> AbstractObservationSource

Build one source from a [[output.observations.sources]] table. Unknown keys and invalid choices fail with an ArgumentError naming the table.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sources.pressure_unit_scale Method
julia
pressure_unit_scale(units, label) -> Float64

Scale a declared pressure unit (Pa, hPa/mbar or kPa) to pascals. Whitespace and case are ignored; absent or unknown units raise ArgumentError.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sources.read_observation_requests Method
julia
read_observation_requests(source, source_index, origin, dates) -> (soundings, sites)

Expand the source's path template for the run days and read every file into SoundingRequests and SiteRequests (one of the two is empty, depending on the source mode). Times are Float64 seconds since origin. Rows with fill values or impossible coordinates are skipped; a source that resolves to no file at all logs a warning.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sources.read_oco2_retrieval_columns Method
julia
read_oco2_retrieval_columns(ds, rows; label = "OCO-2 file") -> Vector{RetrievalColumn{HatLevelProjection}}

The retrieval of records rows (1-based indices along sounding_id) of an open OCO-2 or OCO-3 Lite file or OCO-2 v11 MIP 10-second file, as level columns (RetrievalColumn with HatLevelProjection): the profile values of these retrievals sit on 20 levels with the profile linear in pressure between them. Read per record:

  • the level pressures: pressure_levels (levels, sounding) (Lite files) or sigma_levels (levels) times psurf (sounding) (MIP files), converted to Pa with their units (hPa);

  • pressure_weight, xco2_averaging_kernel (normalized, used as it is, not multiplied by the weights) and co2_profile_apriori (converted to mol/mol with its units, ppm);

  • xco2_apriori, the prior column, when the file has it (converted to mol/mol): the column is then Xa+∑jhjaj(cj−xa,j). For the 10-s averages it differs from ∑jhjxa,j (the weights and the prior were averaged separately) by up to about 0.01 ppm.

The files store the levels from space to the surface; each record is turned surface first (by its pressures, so either order is read correctly). The surface pressure is the bottom level. Every field must be finite and pass the RetrievalColumn checks (weights summing to 1); an invalid record is an error naming its sounding_id.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sources.record_height_above_ground Method
julia
record_height_above_ground(intake_height, altitude, elevation) -> Float64

Height above the ground (m) that a record states by itself: its intake height when finite, else its altitude (m above sea level) minus its ground elevation (m above sea level) when both are finite, else NaN. Evaluated per record: ObsPack files fill intake_height and elevation row by row (the OCO-2 MIP v5.0.1 daily files leave both as fill on aircraft and AirCore rows).

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sources.site_active Method

Whether a site is sampled at the window end t (seconds after the origin).

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sources.valid_pressure Method
julia
valid_pressure(p) -> Bool

Whether a record pressure (Pa) can place the record: finite and positive. A pressure at or below zero is an undeclared fill value (-999.9 hPa) and is treated as absent.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling Module

Sampling for observation columns and sampling.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.DEFAULT_VERTICAL_COORDINATES Constant

Height above the true ground first, then pressure: vertical_coordinates = ["height_above_ground", "pressure"].

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.HEIGHT_METHOD_NOT_SAMPLED Constant

Code written for a site outside its time range (no heights computed).

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.INTERP_FLAG_CODES Constant

Integer interp_flag codes of point-event rows: blended between two window ends, sampled one-sided at the later end (window length changed between binaries), or taken from the nearest window end (nearest_window mode).

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.VERTICAL_PLACEMENT_CODES Constant

Integer vertical_placement codes of the observation files, the method that placed each request (see vertical_placement_codes_description):

CodeNameLayer chosen by
0record_heightthe record's height above ground (intake_height, or altitude − elevation)
1altitude_minus_demaltitude − DEM ground elevation at the point
2pressurethe record's pressure against the interface pressures of the pressure_basis (total by default)
3absolute_altitudealtitude against model surface height + layer heights (absolute_altitude_above_agl_m)
4lowest_layerno vertical coordinate, for sources whose records are column or surface products
source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.AboveGroundPlacement Type

Every record at its height above the ground, measured up from the model surface (default).

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.AbsoluteAltitudeAbove Type
julia
AbsoluteAltitudeAbove(min_height_agl_m)

absolute_altitude_above_agl_m = h: records at least h m above the ground (free-tropospheric aircraft and AirCore samples) are placed by their pressure when the record has one, else by their altitude above sea level against the model's geopotential heights (model surface height plus layer heights). The altitude is the record's altitude, else its ground elevation (the record's, else the DEM's) plus its intake_height; a record with neither keeps its height above the ground. Records below h keep AboveGroundPlacement. Needs a model surface height (surface_height_file).

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.AbstractAltitudePlacement Type

How records that carry an altitude are placed once their height above the ground is known.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.AbstractCellLocator Type
julia
AbstractCellLocator

Per-topology containing-cell lookup. The interface is locate(loc, lon, lat) ; locators are immutable and locate is pure, so they may be shared across threads.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.AbstractLayerTemperature Type

How the layer temperature for hypsometric heights is obtained.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.AbstractMissingHeightRule Type
julia
AbstractMissingHeightRule

What a source's records mean when they give no vertical coordinate at all (no intake_height, altitude or pressure), chosen by the source type (missing_height_rule): LowestLayerWithoutHeight or UnplacedWithoutHeight.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.AbstractModelSurfaceHeight Type
julia
AbstractModelSurfaceHeight

Surface height of the model grid (m above sea level): the ground the model's layer heights are measured from. NoModelSurfaceHeight (default) or ModelSurfaceHeight, read from a per-grid dataset by GriddedIO.read_model_surface_height. Query it with model_surface_height.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.AbstractObservationOutput Type

Parsed [output.observations]: either NoObservationOutput or a spec.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.AbstractObservationStream Type
julia
AbstractObservationStream

Append-only NetCDF sink with the snapshot-stream contract. Concrete streams have path, dataset, count, closed, failed, and queue fields; writes are queued closures op(stream) that run under the shared NetCDF lock.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.AbstractObservationTimeInterpolation Type

How point events are placed in time between met-window ends.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.AbstractPlacementCoordinate Type
julia
AbstractPlacementCoordinate

A vertical coordinate that can place a record in the model column: HeightAboveGroundCoordinate or PressureCoordinate. VerticalPlacementSpec lists the coordinates a run uses in preference order (vertical_coordinates); resolve_placement places each record by the first one it can.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.AbstractPointElevation Type
julia
AbstractPointElevation

Ground elevation (m above sea level) at a point, from a high-resolution digital elevation model: NoPointElevation (default) or GriddedIO.LatLonPointElevation (GriddedIO.read_point_elevation). Query it with point_elevation.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.AbstractPressureBasis Type
julia
AbstractPressureBasis

The vertical basis of a column's placement (pressure_basis), one choice for the interface pressures a pressure-placed record (or an averaging-kernel column) is compared with and for the hypsometric layer heights a record placed by height is compared with: TotalFromHumidity (default) or DryInterfaces. A record's pressure is the total (ambient) pressure, dry air plus water vapour. The air mass of a dry-basis run gives dry interface pressures, pk+1/2=pk−1/2+gmk/A (the weight of the dry air above), which are lower than the total pressure at the same interface by the weight of the water vapour above it: about 0.5 % of the surface pressure for 50 kg m⁻² of precipitable water. The hydrostatic layer thickness is (RdTv/g)ln⁡(pk+1/2/pk−1/2) with total pressures and the virtual temperature Tv=T(1+0.61q); dry pressures and T put heights in a humid boundary layer about 2 % low.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.AbstractUnplacedPolicy Type

What the sampler does with requests it cannot place in the column.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.CellLocation Type
julia
CellLocation

Containing model cell for an observation point. cell is the topology's native flat cell index (lat-lon i + (j-1)Nx, reduced Gaussian cell_index, cubed sphere i + (j-1)Nc within panel). column is the linear column index into the device slab holding this topology's state, including the cubed-sphere halo offset, so a gather can address storage[column + (k-1) * ncolumns]. Indices are plain Int so they can be passed straight to Grids helpers. Device index buffers may narrow column to Int32 (every supported resolution fits) but must widen again before multiplying by ncolumns. lon/lat are the cell-centre coordinates in the mesh's own longitude convention (lat-lon follows the mesh interval; reduced Gaussian and cubed sphere use [0, 360)).

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.ConstantLayerTemperature Type

One temperature for every layer (fallback when the binary carries none).

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.DryInterfaces Type

pressure_basis = "dry": compare a record's pressure with the dry interface pressures pk+1/2=pk−1/2+gmk/A of a dry-basis run, and its height with the hypsometric heights on them with the layer temperature T, zk−1/2=zk+1/2+(RdTk/g)ln⁡(pk+1/2/pk−1/2), for runs whose binaries carry no humidity (the sampler's only rule before issue #20). Both are approximations. The dry interfaces lie at lower pressure than the total ones, so a record can be placed one or more layers lower in the column than its total pressure says, most likely near the surface where the vapour weight above an interface is largest and the layers are thinnest. The heights are low by the dry pressure ratio (−q plus the vapour weight above over the pressure) and by T against Tv (−0.61q): about 2 % in a humid tropical boundary layer (q = 16 g/kg), 6 m at a 300 m intake. Not available on a moist-basis run.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.ErrorOnUnplaced Type

unplaced_records = "error" (default): building the sampler fails, naming the requests.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.GatherPlan Type
julia
GatherPlan(cells, npanel)

Gather order for a batch of cell locations: columns grouped by panel (the cubed sphere needs one contiguous run per panel), the per-panel ranges, and position[i], the gather slot of request i.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.HeightAboveGroundCoordinate Type

"height_above_ground": the record's height h above the true ground, the intake_height, else altitude − elevation, else altitude minus the DEM ground elevation at the point, measured up from the model surface with the model's hypsometric layer heights (vertical_placement codes record_height and altitude_minus_dem).

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.LinearWindowInterpolation Type

Blend the two met-window-end samples bracketing each sounding time (default).

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.LowestLayerWithoutHeight Type

The record is a column or surface product: it is sampled in the lowest layer (vertical_placement = lowest_layer). OCO-2 soundings (their value is the column; the intake value is the surface layer) and table rows without height columns (surface points).

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.ModelSurfaceHeight Type
julia
ModelSurfaceHeight(field, path)

Per-cell surface height of the model grid (m above sea level), in the mesh's native layout: an (Nx, Ny) matrix on a lat-lon mesh, a vector over the cells on a reduced Gaussian mesh, a 6-tuple of (Nc, Nc) panels on the cubed sphere. path is the per-grid dataset it came from (written to the observation files as provenance).

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.NearestWindowSampling Type

Use the single met-window-end sample nearest to each sounding time.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.NoModelSurfaceHeight Type

No model surface height configured; model_surface_height returns NaN.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.NoObservationOutput Type

Default when [output.observations] is absent or enabled = false.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.NoObservationSampler Type

No-op sampler installed when observation output is absent or disabled.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.NoPointElevation Type

No DEM configured; point_elevation returns NaN.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.ObservationCounters Type

Running totals reported in the summary attributes and the end-of-run log.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.ObservationGatherBuffers Type
julia
ObservationGatherBuffers(reference, nlevel, slots; capacity = 1024)

Grow-only scratch for gather_columns!. reference is any state array; device buffers are allocated with similar(reference, …) so they live on the same backend. slots are the tracer storage indices to gather (see tracer_index); an empty slots gathers a single field (see gather_field!). Host mirrors air_host (nlevel, capacity) and tracers_host (nlevel, nslots, capacity) keep the state element type and are valid in columns 1:n after a gather of n requests.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.ObservationOutputSpec Type
julia
ObservationOutputSpec

Parsed [output.observations] table. path is a template: _soundings or _sites is inserted before the extension and, with daily partitions, {date} / {YYYYMMDD} / {day} are substituted per input binary exactly as for snapshot output. tracers === nothing means every model tracer. start_time is only consulted when [input].start_date is absent. placement is the VerticalPlacementSpec.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.ObservationSampler Type
julia
ObservationSampler

Runtime state of observation sampling: the located and vertically placed point events and sites, whether the column's heights and pressures need the humidity, device gather buffers, the held first samples of events awaiting their second sample, the open (and retired daily) output streams, and counters. Built by build_observation_sampler.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.ObservationTerrain Type
julia
ObservationTerrain(; model_surface = NoModelSurfaceHeight(), dem = NoPointElevation())

The static ground fields observation placement may use: the model-grid surface height (AbstractModelSurfaceHeight) and a point DEM (AbstractPointElevation). The runner builds it from [output.observations] through GriddedIO and passes it to build_observation_sampler.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.PendingSoundings Type

Soundings sampled at the previous window end, waiting for their second sample.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.PlacementColumn Type
julia
PlacementColumn(nlevel)

Scratch for column_layer! and sample_column_layer! on a column of nlevel layers: p_half receives the interface pressures of the pressure basis (those a pressure placement is compared with, and the total pressures of the heights), and humidity holds the column's specific humidity (k = 1 at the top), which the caller fills when the pressure basis needs it (needs_column_humidity).

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.PressureCoordinate Type

"pressure": the record's pressure (ObsPack pressure, a total pressure) against the column's interface pressures, built as the AbstractPressureBasis says (vertical_placement code pressure).

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.ProfileLayerTemperature Type

Per-layer temperatures, kelvin[k] with k = 1 at the top.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.SiteNetCDFStream Type
julia
SiteNetCDFStream(path, mesh, nlevel, tracer_names, sites, cells, placements; mass_basis, origin,
                 deflate_level, write_profiles, attributes)

Append-only station sink: one record per met-window end with, per site, the mixing ratio in the layer containing the intake height (<tracer>_intake), the lowest-layer value (<tracer>_surface), the chosen layer and its bounds, surface pressure, and optionally the full profiles (<tracer>, p_half, air mass). Sites outside their TimeRange are written as NaN with intake_level = 0. placements holds each site's VerticalPlacement, written as static metadata.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.SiteRecord Type
julia
SiteRecord(time, nsite, nlevel, ntracer; profiles)

One time record for every site, allocated uninitialised for the sampler to fill. values (intake layer) and surface_values are (nsite, ntracer); with profiles = true the record also carries p_half (nlevel + 1, nsite), air_mass_per_area (nlevel, nsite) and profiles (nlevel, nsite, ntracer), otherwise those arrays are empty.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.SkipUnplaced Type

unplaced_records = "skip": such requests are dropped and counted (n_unplaced_* attributes).

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.SoundingBatch Type
julia
SoundingBatch(; ids, sources, times, latitudes, longitudes, cells, sample_time_prev,
              sample_time_next, weights, flags, p_half, air_mass_per_area, tracers,
              column_means, elevations, intake_heights, altitudes, pressures, placements,
              intake_levels, layer_bottom, layer_top, height_methods, intake_values,
              retrieval_values = nothing)

Columns of one emitted batch of n events. Profiles are (nlevel, n), p_half is (nlevel + 1, n), tracers (nlevel, ntracer, n), column means and intake values (ntracer, n). Times are seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC. elevations, intake_heights, altitudes and pressures are the records' own values; placements the VerticalPlacement of each row. retrieval_values are the averaging-kernel columns (n_retrieval_tracers, n) of a sampler with averaging-kernel output (NaN where a row has none), or nothing.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.SoundingNetCDFStream Type
julia
SoundingNetCDFStream(path, mesh, nlevel, tracer_names; mass_basis, origin, deflate_level, attributes)

Append-only point-event sink. Each appended batch writes one row per event: identity, time, location, containing cell, bracketing sample times and weight, interface pressures, per-layer air mass per area, each tracer's mixing-ratio profile and column mean, and the intake-layer value. With retrieval_tracers (sources with averaging-kernel columns) it also writes <tracer>_ak_column (Float64, NaN for rows without a retrieval).

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.SurfaceLapseTemperature Type

2 m temperature with a constant lapse rate (K m⁻¹) above the surface, by default STANDARD_LAPSE_RATE, floored at the standard-atmosphere tropopause temperature STANDARD_TROPOPAUSE_TEMPERATURE so tall columns stay physical.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.TotalFromHumidity Type

pressure_basis = "total" (default): compare a record's pressure with the column's total interface pressures, and a record's height with the hypsometric heights of moist air on them. Specific humidity qk (kg of water vapour per kg of moist air) makes the moist air mass of layer k mk/(1−qk) for a dry air mass mk (kg), so on a dry-basis run the hydrostatic total pressures and the interface heights above the model surface are

p1/2=ptop,pk+1/2=pk−1/2+gmkA(1−qk),zk−1/2=zk+1/2+RdTk(1+cqk)gln⁡pk+1/2pk−1/2,

with zN+1/2=0, Tk the layer temperature, c=Rv/Rd−1 (VIRTUAL_TEMPERATURE_FACTOR, 0.61) and Tk(1+cqk) the virtual temperature (exact for layers of uniform T and q), A the cell area and ptop the pure-pressure model-top interface A_ifc[1], a total pressure in the met model's hybrid coordinate (level 1 is the top). This inverts the preprocessing's dry conversion Δpdry=(1−q)Δp. On merged or remapped levels the binary carries a dry-mass-weighted q, so the inverse is not exact there; on the golden pre_ll72 binary (ERA5 L137 merged to 34 levels) the rebuilt total surface pressure differs from the stored one by −0.012 Pa on average and 0.125 Pa at most, where the dry interfaces are 169 Pa low on average and 700 Pa at worst. The humidity is the binary's layer-mean specific humidity at the sampled boundary: qv_start / qv_end of lat-lon binaries preprocessed with output.include_qv = true; on cubed-sphere binaries with the GCHP VDIFF payload the window-start VDIFF qv of the next window (the run's last window end takes the ended window's, one window old). Reduced-Gaussian binaries, and cubed-sphere binaries without the VDIFF payload, carry no humidity. On a moist-basis run the air mass already includes the vapour and its interfaces are total pressures without humidity; the heights there use T (no humidity is gathered, so the virtual-temperature term, about 1 % of the heights in a humid boundary layer, is neglected). A dry-basis run whose binaries do not all carry humidity cannot build them: building a sampler with any request, whatever its vertical coordinate (every row reports its layer's heights), then fails unless pressure_basis = "dry".

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.UnplacedWithoutHeight Type

The record should state a height and does not: it cannot be placed (unplaced_records). ObsPack records, where every platform carries a height.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.VerticalPlacement Type
julia
VerticalPlacement(method, height_agl_m, pressure_pa, model_surface_m)

How one request is placed in the column, resolved once by resolve_placement: method is a VERTICAL_PLACEMENT_CODES code; height_agl_m the height above the model surface that selects the layer (NaN for pressure and lowest-layer placement); pressure_pa the pressure that selects it (pressure placement only); model_surface_m the model surface height of the cell (NaN without a surface-height dataset).

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.VerticalPlacementSpec Type
julia
VerticalPlacementSpec(; surface_height_file = nothing, dem_file = nothing, dem_variable = "z",
                        unplaced = ErrorOnUnplaced(), altitude_placement = AboveGroundPlacement(),
                        coordinates = DEFAULT_VERTICAL_COORDINATES,
                        pressure_basis = TotalFromHumidity())

The vertical-placement settings of [output.observations]: the per-grid model surface height dataset, an optional point DEM (file and variable), the AbstractUnplacedPolicy, the AbstractAltitudePlacement, the AbstractPlacementCoordinates in preference order (a non-empty tuple without repeats; by default height above ground, then pressure), and the AbstractPressureBasis of pressure placement.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.VirtualLayerTemperature Type
julia
VirtualLayerTemperature(temperature, humidity)

The virtual temperature Tv=T(1+cqk) of each layer, from the layer temperature T of the AbstractLayerTemperature temperature and the specific humidity humidity[k] (kg kg⁻¹ of moist air, k = 1 at the top), with c = VIRTUAL_TEMPERATURE_FACTOR (Rv/Rd−1, the model's 0.61, as in the diffusion layer thicknesses). Moist air of temperature T has the density of dry air at Tv, so the hypsometric thickness of a layer between total pressures is (RdTv/g)ln⁡(pk+1/2/pk−1/2) (placement_heights! with TotalFromHumidity). The humidity is used as it is, the same values as the total pressures.

AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.append_site_record! Method
julia
append_site_record!(stream, record) -> count

Queue one met-window-end record for every site, then flush if the NetCDF lock is free; each flushed record is synced before completed_times is published. Returns the new reserved record count.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.append_soundings! Method
julia
append_soundings!(stream, batch) -> count

Queue batch after the rows already reserved, then flush if the NetCDF lock is free; each flushed batch is synced before completed_soundings is published. Returns the new reserved row count.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.begin_observation_day! Method
julia
begin_observation_day!(sampler, date_label, day_index)

Called by the runner before the first window boundary of each input binary. Single-file runs open their files on the first call; daily runs close the previous day's files and open the next pair. Rows are written to the files open at emission time. A binary's last window ends at the next day's 00:00, which is still observed before the next binary opens: with linear interpolation a sounding lands in the file of its own day, and each day's sites file ends with the 00:00 sample of the next day (the first file also holds the initial state at t = 0). With nearest_window, soundings in the first half window after 00:00 are emitted at that boundary and land in the previous day's file.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.below_ground Method
julia
below_ground(placement::VerticalPlacement) -> Bool

Whether a placement by height above the ground (record_height, altitude_minus_dem) puts the record more than BELOW_GROUND_TOLERANCE_M (100 m) below the ground. Such records are sampled in the lowest layer; the sampler counts them and warns.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.build_observation_sampler Method
julia
build_observation_sampler(spec, state, grid; origin, window_seconds, halo_width,
                          terrain = ObservationTerrain(), has_humidity = false)

Read every source for the days covering window_seconds (seconds after origin, half-open), locate the requests on grid.horizontal, place each in the column (resolve_placement with the static ground fields of terrain, see ObservationTerrain), and prepare the device gather buffers. Requests that cannot be placed fail the build or are skipped and counted, as spec.placement.unplaced says. has_humidity says whether the run's binaries carry specific humidity: on a dry-basis run every request needs it for the total interface pressures and the virtual-temperature layer heights of TotalFromHumidity (the default spec.placement.pressure_basis; check_pressure_basis), and the build fails without it unless the basis is DryInterfaces; every window end must then pass humidity to observe_window_boundary!. Output files are opened by begin_observation_day!. NoObservationOutput yields NoObservationSampler().

cell_locator(mesh; halo_width) -> AbstractCellLocator

Build the containing-cell locator for mesh. halo_width is the padding of the state arrays that CellLocation.column addresses: lat-lon and reduced-Gaussian state is unpadded; cubed-sphere state defaults to the mesh halo Hp.

AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.check_observation_tracer_names Method

check_observation_tracer_names(names; averaging_kernel_tracers = Symbol[])

AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.check_pressure_basis Method
julia
check_pressure_basis(basis, mass_basis, has_humidity, n_column, label) -> Bool

Check, when the requests are placed, that basis can build the layer heights and interface pressures of n_column requests placed in the column on a run of mass_basis whose binaries carry specific humidity when has_humidity, and return whether sampling needs that humidity (needs_column_humidity with at least one request: TotalFromHumidity on a dry-basis run). Every placed request counts, whatever its coordinate: its layer heights are built (and reported) on the basis. Throws for DryInterfaces on a moist-basis run, and for TotalFromHumidity with requests on a dry-basis run without humidity; label names the config table ("[output.observations]").

AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.column_layer! Method
julia
column_layer!(column::PlacementColumn, placement, z_half, air_column, area, g, p_top, basis, mass_basis) -> Int

Model layer (k = 1 top) of a VerticalPlacement in one column, the rule shared by the forward sampler and any other caller: by height above the model surface on the hypsometric interface heights z_half, or the lowest layer (as placement_layer); a pressure placement against the interface pressures of the AbstractPressureBasis basis, built into column.p_half from air_column (kg per cell, of mass_basis), the cell area (m²), gravity g, the model-top pressure p_top and, for TotalFromHumidity on a dry basis, column.humidity.

finish_observations!(sampler)

Emit events exactly at the final window end, drop events that never received their second sample, write the summary attributes, and warn about anything that was not sampled. Idempotent.

AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.gather_columns! Function
julia
gather_columns!(buf, state, columns, panel_ranges = nothing) -> n

Gather the air mass and the buffered tracer slots of columns (Int32 linear column indices, see CellLocation.column) from state into buf.air_host[:, 1:n] and buf.tracers_host[:, :, 1:n]. Lat-lon and reduced-Gaussian states ignore panel_ranges; cubed-sphere states require columns grouped by panel with panel_ranges[p] giving panel p's run so that the six ranges tile 1:n in order.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.gather_field! Function
julia
gather_field!(buf, field, columns, panel_ranges = nothing) -> n

Gather one per-layer field with the air-mass layout (an array, or a 6-tuple of panel arrays) into buf.air_host[:, 1:n]; buf must have been built with no tracer slots. Used for optional temperature fields.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.intake_layer_index Method
julia
intake_layer_index(z_half, height) -> Int

Layer k with z_half[k+1] <= h < z_half[k] (k = 1 top), h in metres above the model surface. A non-positive height selects the lowest layer; a height above the column top selects layer 1. A NaN height is an ArgumentError: requests without a height are placed explicitly (placement_layer), never by a NaN fallback.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.interface_pressures! Method
julia
interface_pressures!(p_half, air_column, area, g, p_top)

Interface pressures (Pa) from a column of air mass per cell (kg), top down: p_half[1] = p_top, p_half[k+1] = p_half[k] + g·m[k]/area. On a dry-basis state this is the dry partial pressure.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.layer_heights_agl! Method
julia
layer_heights_agl!(z_half, p_half, temperature, g; R_dry = R_DRY_AIR)

Hypsometric interface heights above ground (m) from interface pressures, z_half[end] = 0 at the surface, accumulated upward with the layer temperature from temperature evaluated at the layer's bottom height: zk−1/2=zk+1/2+(RdTk/g)ln⁡(pk+1/2/pk−1/2). Exact for total pressures with the virtual temperature (VirtualLayerTemperature) of layers of uniform Tv; placement_heights! chooses the pressures and the temperature. A non-positive or non-monotone pressure gives an infinite height from that layer upward.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.locate Function
julia
locate(loc::AbstractCellLocator, lon, lat) -> Union{CellLocation, Nothing}

Containing cell of a point given in degrees, in any longitude convention. Returns nothing only when the mesh does not cover the point (regional lat-lon meshes); global meshes always return a cell. Faces follow the half-open convention: a point exactly on a face belongs to the cell to its east or north, except on the mesh's outermost northern and eastern faces. Invalid coordinates (see isvalid_lonlat) throw an ArgumentError.

julia
missing_height_rule(source) -> AbstractMissingHeightRule

How records of source without any vertical coordinate are placed: LowestLayerWithoutHeight for OCO2LiteSource and TableSource, UnplacedWithoutHeight for ObsPackSource.

Per-layer mixing ratio tracer/air, NaN where the carrier mass is not positive.

julia
needs_column_humidity(basis, mass_basis) -> Bool

Whether a column's layer heights and interface pressures on the AbstractPressureBasis basis need its specific humidity: on a dry-basis run TotalFromHumidity builds the total pressures and the virtual temperature from it, for every placement (the heights of sample_column_layer!) and for averaging-kernel columns. DryInterfaces, and a moist-basis run, need none.

Whether observe_window_boundary! needs the specific humidity: the sampler builds its columns' heights and pressures on total pressures (TotalFromHumidity) on a dry-basis run.

AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.observation_output_path Method
julia
observation_output_path(spec, mode, date_label, day_index) -> String

Resolve the file for mode::AbstractObservationMode. _soundings / _sites is inserted before the extension. Daily runs substitute the day template exactly like output_path_for_day; single-file runs substitute it only when the path carries a {date} / {YYYYMMDD} / {day} token, using the first day's label, and otherwise use the path as given.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.observation_output_spec Method
julia
observation_output_spec(output_cfg; partition = nothing)

Parse [output.observations] from the [output] table. Returns NoObservationOutput() when the subtable is absent or enabled = false, otherwise an ObservationOutputSpec. Unknown keys, a missing path or sources, and invalid choices raise ArgumentError. The file partition (one file vs. one per daily binary) follows [output].split unless partition is given; split is only read when observations are enabled.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.observe_window_boundary! Method
julia
observe_window_boundary!(sampler, state, time_seconds; next_window_seconds, temperature = nothing,
                         humidity = nothing)

Sample state at a met-window end time_seconds after the run origin. next_window_seconds is the length of the window that starts now (it sets which soundings receive their first sample). temperature, when given, is a per-layer temperature field (K, k = 1 at the top) used for site layer heights, either with the air-mass layout or, on the cubed sphere, as interior-only panels; otherwise the configured constant applies. humidity is the specific humidity (kg kg⁻¹ of moist air, k = 1 at the top) at this window end, in the same layouts; a sampler that builds its columns on total pressures on a dry-basis run (TotalFromHumidity: the layer heights of every row, pressure placement, averaging-kernel columns) requires it and otherwise ignores it. Call once at t = 0 on the initial state and after every window.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.parse_vertical_placement Method
julia
parse_vertical_placement(cfg, label) -> VerticalPlacementSpec

Parse the vertical-placement keys (VERTICAL_PLACEMENT_KEYS) of the config table cfg, named label in error messages ("[output.observations]"): surface_height_file, dem_file/dem_variable, unplaced_records, absolute_altitude_above_agl_m, vertical_coordinates and pressure_basis. The caller checks for unknown keys. Keys that would have no effect are errors: dem_variable without dem_file, and dem_file or absolute_altitude_above_agl_m (both act on placements by height) when vertical_coordinates leaves out "height_above_ground". pressure_basis applies to every coordinate (the layer heights are built on it too).

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.placement_heights! Method
julia
placement_heights!(z_half, column::PlacementColumn, basis, mass_basis, p_half, air_column, area, g, p_top,
                   temperature) -> z_half

Hypsometric interface heights above the model surface (m, k = 1 top) of one column, on the vertical basis of the AbstractPressureBasis basis (layer_heights_agl!):

  • TotalFromHumidity on a dry basis: the total interface pressures from the dry air mass and the specific humidity column.humidity (total_interface_pressures!, into column.p_half) with the virtual temperature Tv=T(1+0.61qk) of temperature (VirtualLayerTemperature), the hydrostatic thickness of moist air;

  • otherwise the interface pressures of the air mass, p_half (filled by the caller): the dry interfaces with T for DryInterfaces, an approximation that puts heights about 2 % low in a humid boundary layer (the dry pressure ratio and T instead of Tv each about 1 % for q = 16 g/kg), and on a moist-basis run the total interfaces of the moist air mass with T (no humidity is gathered there, so the virtual temperature term, about 1 %, is neglected).

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.placement_layer Method
julia
placement_layer(placement, z_half, p_half) -> Int

Model layer (k = 1 top) of a VerticalPlacement in one sampled column: by height above the model surface (intake_layer_index on the hypsometric interface heights z_half), by pressure (pressure_layer_index on the interface pressures p_half), or the lowest layer.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.placement_pressures! Method
julia
placement_pressures!(p_half, basis, mass_basis, air_column, humidity_column, area, g, p_top) -> p_half

Interface pressures (Pa, k = 1 top) a pressure-placed record is compared with, for a column of air mass per cell (kg) of mass_basis: TotalFromHumidity builds the total pressures from the dry air mass and the specific humidity humidity_column (total_interface_pressures!) on a dry-basis run and takes the moist air mass as it is on a moist-basis run; DryInterfaces gives the dry interfaces of a dry-basis run (interface_pressures!). humidity_column is ignored where no humidity is needed.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.point_elevation Method
julia
point_elevation(dem, lon, lat) -> Float64

Ground elevation (m above sea level) of dem at the point, NaN where the DEM has no value (outside its coverage, fill, or NoPointElevation).

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.pressure_layer_index Method
julia
pressure_layer_index(p_half, p) -> Int

Layer k with p_half[k] <= p < p_half[k+1] (k = 1 top). A pressure at or above the surface interface selects the lowest layer; one below the column top selects layer 1. p must be finite and positive (valid_pressure).

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.resolve_placement Method
julia
resolve_placement(spec::VerticalPlacementSpec, missing_height, request, cell, terrain)
    -> Union{VerticalPlacement, Nothing}

Place a SoundingRequest or SiteRequest in the column of its containing cell by the first of spec.coordinates (AbstractPlacementCoordinate, in preference order) that places it:

  • HeightAboveGroundCoordinate: the record's height above ground h (intake_height, or altitude − elevation with the record's or station's elevation; record_height), else h = altitude minus the DEM ground elevation at the point (altitude_minus_dem). The record is placed h above the model surface.

  • PressureCoordinate: the record's pressure (pressure), when it is valid_pressure (finite and positive).

A record that none of the coordinates place is unplaced (nothing) when it states any vertical coordinate (an intake_height, an altitude, a valid pressure), e.g. an altitude without a ground elevation (no record elevation, no DEM value), or a coordinate the run does not use. One without any vertical coordinate goes to the lowest layer (lowest_layer) under LowestLayerWithoutHeight and is unplaced under UnplacedWithoutHeight (missing_height, from missing_height_rule of the record's source). The model surface height is never used as the true ground.

spec.altitude_placement = AbsoluteAltitudeAbove(h₀) then re-places records placed by a height h≥h0 by their pressure (when pressure is one of the coordinates), else by absolute altitude: the stated altitude, else the ground elevation (the record's, else the DEM value at the point) plus intake_height; a record with neither keeps its height above the ground.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.sample_column_layer! Method
julia
sample_column_layer!(column::PlacementColumn, p_half, z_half, placement, air_column, area, g, p_top,
                     temperature, basis, mass_basis) -> Int

The layer (k = 1 top) of a VerticalPlacement in one sampled column, from the column alone: the interface pressures of the air mass (interface_pressures! into p_half, pk+1/2=pk−1/2+gmk/A from p_top; dry pressures on a dry-basis run), the hypsometric interface heights above the model surface on the vertical basis of basis (placement_heights! into z_half, with the AbstractLayerTemperature temperature: total pressures and virtual temperature for TotalFromHumidity on a dry basis), then column_layer!. column.humidity must hold the column's specific humidity whenever the basis needs it (needs_column_humidity), for every placement, since the heights use it. The forward observation sampler and the inversion's placed point observations both choose their layers with this function.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.samples_observations Method

Whether the runner must visit every met-window end for this sampler.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.terrain_source Method
julia
terrain_source(field) -> String

Where a terrain field came from, written to the observation files: the file path, "" for NoModelSurfaceHeight / NoPointElevation. Concrete DEM types add a method.

source
AtmosTransport.Observations.Sampling.total_interface_pressures! Method
julia
total_interface_pressures!(p_half, dry_air_column, humidity_column, area, g, p_top)

Total (dry air plus water vapour) interface pressures (Pa) from a column of dry air mass per cell (kg) and the layers' specific humidity (kg of vapour per kg of moist air), top down: p_half[1] = p_top, p_half[k+1] = p_half[k] + g·m[k] / (area·(1 − q[k])), the hydrostatic weight of the moist air m[k]/(1 − q[k]) (see TotalFromHumidity). Every q must be finite and below 1; small negative values (interpolation undershoot) are used as they are.

Visualization ​

AtmosTransport.Visualization lives in src/Extras/Visualization/. It is non-core, has no tests, and is intended to become its own package. The Makie extension stays in ext/AtmosTransportMakieExt.jl, Julia's extension location. Core modules never import Visualization.

Field selection uses typed values. Pass ColumnMean(), ColumnSum(), LevelSlice(), or SurfaceSlice() as the transform keyword to fieldview; LevelSlice() also requires level. Pass NativeUnit() or PPMUnit() as unit, and pass AllFrames() to frame_indices to select every frame. These selectors are exported by AtmosTransport.Visualization, not by the top-level module. For example:

julia
using AtmosTransport.Visualization
snapshot = open_snapshot("output.nc")
surface = fieldview(snapshot, :co2; transform=SurfaceSlice(), time=1,
                    unit=PPMUnit())
levels = fieldview(snapshot, :co2; transform=LevelSlice(), level=10, time=1)
AtmosTransport.Visualization Module
julia
Visualization

Topology-aware snapshot visualization support.

This module owns the lightweight data layer only: snapshot discovery, field views, unit scaling, and topology-aware rasterization for quick maps. Makie plotting lives in AtmosTransportMakieExt so the model/runtime does not pay a plotting load cost unless a Makie backend is explicitly loaded.

CubedSphereSnapshotTopology(Nc, nlevel, panel_convention[, definition])

Cubed-sphere snapshot geometry. Values are stored as (Xdim, Ydim, nf) for a single horizontal field, with nf == 6. definition is the mesh the snapshot was written on (coordinate and center laws, panel convention, longitude offset); it defaults to the panel convention's standard definition.
